LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard variable assignments and function definitions. During `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, only the top-level (global) scope is evaluated, which in this case consists of metadata declarations (pkgname, pkgver, etc.), array definitions (arch, depends, source, sha256sums), and no immediate command substitutions or executable statements. The `source` array references a predictable tarball URL based on the declared pkgver and upstream GitHub repository, which is a normal pattern. The sha256sums array is present with a fixed hash, though it will be updated later—this does not affect safety during parsing. There are no top-level commands, downloads, or data exfiltration attempts executed at parse time. Functions like `check()` and `package()` are defined but not executed during this phase and are out of scope for this narrow gate.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No dangerous code executes during sourcing.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Arch Linux package build process for the `kreuzer` application, a terminal-based financial tracker. It fetches the source code from the project's official GitHub repository using a tagged release archive, which is a common and expected practice. The `sha256sums` array contains a placeholder hash that will be updated by `updpkgsums` once the tag is pushed—this is normal during development and not inherently unsafe, as the hash will be set before release.

The build process consists of running `make test` in the `check()` function and installing files via `make install` in the `package()` function, both within the extracted source directory. These are standard operations that delegate to the upstream build system. The package depends only on common, trusted core utilities (bash, gawk, coreutils, etc.), which are reasonable for a shell-based application. There are no network operations, file modifications outside the package directory, or execution of downloaded code during build or install.

No obfuscated commands, suspicious downloads, or unsafe operations (such as `curl|bash`, `eval`, or data exfiltration) are present. The `test -f man/kreuzer.1` check ensures a generated man page exists before installation, which is a defensive measure for correctness, not a security risk. All actions are transparent and aligned with the application's purpose.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard PKGBUILD with no malicious content</summary>
</security_assessment>

It lists standard package information such as name, version, dependencies, source URL, and checksum. The source is a tagged release from the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/shashotoNur/kreuzer), specifically version `v0.1.0`, which matches the `pkgver`. The `sha256sums` field contains a valid checksum for the source tarball, indicating that the package maintainers intend to verify the integrity of the downloaded source. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious network locations, or unexpected commands. All dependencies are common Unix utilities (bash, gawk, coreutils, etc.), which are reasonable for a shell-based terminal application. No scripts or executable logic are present in this file — it is purely declarative metadata. Therefore, no malicious or suspicious behavior can be inferred from this file.
</details>
